adjudication.method: Operator adjudication against the complete source reviews and exact reviewed code. SAME_ROOT means one architectural remediation would plausibly address both manifestations; DIFFERENT_ROOT means it would not; AMBIGUOUS marks mixed or boundary-dependent cases.
adjudication.limitation: No second human adjudicator was available; AMBIGUOUS is used rather than forcing disputed boundaries.

pairs.adjudicationRationale: Both report non-activating output truncation whose only practical effect is a runtime import and test mock.
Both report recurrence clustering and remediation using inconsistent identity boundaries.
Both report an extension export surface created for tests rather than consumers.
Both report a checkpoint in one root class globally blocking remediation for unrelated classes.
Both report record transitions treating an event SHA as the assessment head.
Both report a whole-package mock hiding failures in the real runtime import surface.
A checkpoint lacking a resolution lifecycle is distinct from a checkpoint applying at excessive scope.
Unstable reviewer-supplied classification text is distinct from inconsistent identity keys inside recurrence operations.
Dead output truncation is distinct from an unnecessarily broad export surface.
An inert severity variant is distinct from ordering recurrence by insertion rather than commit ancestry.
Tuple serialization as a map key is distinct from quadratic cloning on append.
Misnaming older open findings as stale is distinct from using event SHAs as head SHAs.
Ordering events without ancestry is distinct from choosing event-log persistence where a snapshot suffices.
Unbounded display aggregation is distinct from module export leakage.
Missing lifecycle resolution is distinct from coupling persisted replay to mutable validation rules.
Unstable semantic identity labels are distinct from unreachable output truncation.
A missing honest test seam is distinct from exposing test-only APIs to consumers.
Reporting only one qualifying cluster is distinct from misclassifying older open findings as stale.
Quadratic event cloning is distinct from the architectural choice of event-log persistence.
Unbounded abstraction display joining is distinct from assessment head identity.
An inert schema branch is distinct from a serialized compound map key.
Finding-state terminology is distinct from global checkpoint scope.
Insertion-order recurrence is distinct from an inconsistently scoped SHA-reuse guard.
Checkpoint lifecycle is distinct from module export surface.
Both concern replay validation, but one is persistence compatibility and the other is redundant implementation; whether one remediation addresses both depends on the chosen replay boundary.
Both concern strict replay, but mutable-rule coupling and choosing an event log over a snapshot may require different architectural changes.
F19 contains both global checkpoint scope and single-cluster visibility, so it partially overlaps F07 but is not a clean atomic root.
Both expose inconsistent identity scope, but one concerns root/abstraction identity and the other review/remediation SHA validity.
